title: Affine representation of a linear threshold function
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\bbr$ be a linear threshold function, meaning it is the threshold of a multilinear polynomial of degree at most one, with threshold sign equal to $1$ on nonnegative inputs and $-1$ on negative inputs. Then there are $c\in\bbr$ and coefficients $a_i\in\bbr$ for $i\in[n]$ such that, for every $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, \[f(x)=\sigma\!\left(c+\sum_{i\in[n]}a_i(-1)^{x_i}\right),\] where $\sigma(r)=1$ for $r\ge0$ and $\sigma(r)=-1$ for $r<0$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the Boolean cube
$f$ is a polynomial threshold function of degree at most one
replaced: Let $n\ge0$ and give $\{0,1\}^n$ uniform probability; write $\mathbb E$ for expectation. Put $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E[h\chi_S]$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ and real cube functions $h$. Write $\operatorname{sgn}_+(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$. If $f$ is the sign $\operatorname{sgn}_+(P)$ of a Walsh polynomial $P$ whose coefficients vanish on sets larger than one, then there exist real $c$ and $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ such that $f(x)=\operatorname{sgn}_+(c+\sum_i a_i(-1)^{x_i})$ for every $x$.
